scenes.heading: Event Driven Architecture
scenes.narration: Event-driven architecture connects systems through events, letting components react to changes without tight coupling.

scenes.heading: Its defining traits
bullets: Producers emit events without knowing consumers.
Loose coupling makes systems easy to evolve.
An event broker mediates the flow.
scenes.narration: Producers simply announce that something happened, unaware of who might care. Consumers subscribe and react on their own schedule, independent of the producer. This loose coupling lets teams add or change consumers freely, with a broker in the middle routing events reliably.

scenes.heading: Request-driven vs event-driven
scenes.narration: In a request-driven design, a service calls another and waits, binding the two tightly together. In an event-driven design, a producer emits an event and moves on, while consumers react whenever they can. That asynchrony scales better and lets each part evolve without breaking its neighbors.

scenes.heading: An event's path
scenes.narration: When a producer detects a change, it publishes an event to a broker. The broker durably stores and routes that event to whichever topics apply. Multiple consumers subscribed to those topics each receive it and react in their own way, entirely decoupled from the producer.

scenes.text: Event-driven architecture uses a broker so producers and consumers stay decoupled, reacting to events asynchronously and independently.
scenes.narration: The loose coupling of events is what lets large systems grow and change without every component having to know about every other.
